title: In Ranchi, a protest against tree felling ends in detentions

ai.summary: Protesters in Ranchi detained by police during demonstration against proposed road expansion that would felling trees and displace Adivasi communities.

facts.claim: More than a dozen people, including several activists, were detained by police in Ranchi on Wednesday during a protest against the proposed felling of trees and the displacement of Adivasi bastis for a 10-lane road project.
facts.quote: More than a dozen people, including several activists, were detained by police in Ranchi on Wednesday during a protest against the proposed felling of trees and the displacement of Adivasi bastis for a 10-lane road project.

facts.claim: Protesters said they were standing at a distance from one another and were not obstructing traffic.
facts.quote: Protesters said they were standing at a distance from one another and were not obstructing traffic.

facts.claim: Shailesh Krishna, an activist who has been raising the issue of the proposed tree-felling, said the existing four-lane road was adequate and there was no need to expand it into a 10-lane road.
facts.quote: Shailesh Krishna, an activist who has been raising the issue of the proposed tree-felling, said the existing four-lane road was adequate and there was no need to expand it into a 10-lane road.

facts.claim: According to a petition filed on Wednesday by advocates Piyushita Tudu and Shailesh Poddar, approximately 7,000 trees would have to be felled to expand a 4–5 km stretch into a 10-lane road.
facts.quote: According to a petition filed on Wednesday by advocates Piyushita Tudu and Shailesh Poddar, approximately 7,000 trees would have to be felled to expand a 4–5 km stretch into a 10-lane road.

facts.claim: Activist Siraj Dutta said the proposed road expansion would also affect settlements along the route.
facts.quote: Activist Siraj Dutta said the proposed road expansion would also affect settlements along the route.

facts.claim: Dutta also questioned the police action, claiming that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was not applicable at the spot where they were protesting.
facts.quote: Dutta also questioned the police action, claiming that Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was not applicable at the spot where they were protesting.

facts.claim: Nayan, one of the two women social workers detained, alleged that police personnel used force against the protesters despite their asking under which law they were being prevented from standing there.
facts.quote: Nayan, one of the two women social workers detained, alleged that police personnel used force against the protesters despite their asking under which law they were being prevented from standing there.

facts.claim: A police official from Tupudana police station said that protests were not allowed within a 1-km radius of the Vidhan Sabha as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were in force.
facts.quote: A police official from Tupudana police station said that protests were not allowed within a 1-km radius of the Vidhan Sabha as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS were in force.
